assessment.scope: Static review of the new Main-authored fixture, its production route/gather/combine path, and the queue/lifetime APIs it exercises.
assessment.novelty: High relative to R971/R972: those audits concern the engine integration and predate this fixture; R974 correctly examines a new test executable.
assessment.redundancy: Low. There is some repeated context about routing and the 8192-row split, but the fixture-specific oracle independence, alias ordering, and host lifetime analysis are new.
assessment.depth: Strong and within the 24576-byte report budget. Source evidence and exclusions are explicit; no research findings are promoted to runtime or performance claims.
factual_corrections: The final output oracle is independent of planner maps because it copies original IDs to oracle_ids and uses them at fixture lines 112 and 139-146. The per-gather comparison is not independent: fixture lines 132-134 use src[offset + row] both to select the gathered input and to compute its expected value. This is a scoped independence gap, not a contradiction in the report.

R974's source-map/expert false-pass mechanism is valid: a bad row or job can alter an expert output yet remain equal after weighted FP32 accumulation and final BF16 store at native16.cpp:148-157. No GPU result currently establishes whether the selected negative-source/negative-slot mutations trigger the oracle.

R974 correctly treats malformed upper source indices as untested: gather_rows16 maps negative rows to zero but dereferences nonnegative rows without an upper bound at postops.cpp:239-247. Current fixture faults stay in range.

The route shape description is accurate for concentrated cases: rows > 8192 asserts ten experts each have rows entries and exactly twenty jobs at fixture lines 82-86. balanced16384 has 320 occurrences per expert by the input formula, but only the concentrated counts/job total are asserted directly.

findings.title: Bind the pre-combine witness to an independently derived original route
evidence: tests/sycl/moe_window.cpp:132-135 derives the expected gathered row from the same device src map being exercised; job.expert supplies the witness expert.
tests/sycl/moe_window.cpp:139-147 checks only after pn::combine and computes expected output from original IDs.
src/prefill/sycl/native16.cpp:148-157 accumulates weighted expert outputs in FP32 and stores BF16, so a wrong source/expert contribution can be hidden by final rounding.
include/strata/prefill/moe_window_routes.hpp:85-95 defines the map under test and its stable ordering; it must not be the source of the fixture's expected map.
findings.failure_mode: The gather check can accept a wrong source map if gather faithfully reads that wrong row. The final oracle catches many such cases, but not all: the weighted change may round to the same BF16 output. A wrong expert/job result has the same post-combine masking risk.
minimal_repair: From original IDs alone, build test-side expected route slots/source tokens (for example, stable-sort route indices by expert and original route index); do not read plan.source_rows(), plan.slot_map(), plan.offsets(), or plan.jobs() to form expected values.
Before writing the synthetic witness, compare each gathered row against input_bits(expected_source_token, column, salt), and compare its job expert against the expected expert for that destination.

Before combine, check actual slot values are in [0,routes) and equal expected slots; then compare down[expected_slot, column] directly with witness(input_bits(original_token, column, salt), original_expert). Use the trusted expected slot for this read so a corrupted slot cannot redirect the oracle.
findings.classification: Fixture false-pass coverage gap; no production routing defect established.

evidence: tests/sycl/moe_window.cpp:75-112 constructs ids, plan, and every Allocation before arming DraftUploadGuard; no queued work precedes the lease.

tests/sycl/moe_window.cpp:95-149 uses rt->compute() for uploads, fixture kernels, production gather/combine, error readback, and checked drain; the same in-order queue makes mixed-output aliasing after final gather ordered.
src/sycl/runtime.cpp:78-95 creates compute_ as in_order; runtime.cpp:112-130 waits both queues and rethrows sticky errors; launch.hpp:47-63 binds the passed queue and requires in_order.
draft_uploads.hpp:67-79 drains before stack owners unwind and fail-stops if completion cannot be proved; fixture lines 43-52 does the same for stack readback destinations.
Khronos SYCL 2020 rev.11 section 4.9.4.3 permits host pointers to queue::memcpy; ids and plan vectors remain live through rt->wait().
findings.classification: Static source assessment only; it does not prove any device execution.

findings.title: Invalid-map sentinels and arbitrary out-of-range reads are not generated
evidence: tests/sycl/moe_window.cpp:114-115 only changes source/slot values to other in-range values.
postops.cpp:245-247 has no upper source-row bound; edge canaries guard writes, not reads.
findings.recommendation: Keep malformed-map coverage separate. If added, validate source row bounds before enqueueing gather so no invalid read is issued; do not present the current in-range mutation controls as coverage of malformed source indices.

findings.title: Synthetic fixture does not qualify real model or broad context correctness
evidence: Fixture lines 1-2 and 185 state its synthetic witness and no model/GEMM/state/speed claim.
src/prefill/moe_window.inc:129-151 shows the production expert dequant/GEMM and residual write stages absent from the fixture.
findings.recommendation: Keep real GEMM/dequant, router, recurrent/state paths, attention/PLE/GDN/QSA/HC/MTP, physical 262144-context consume, saved-session RESTORE, task quality, and performance as separate pending qualification gates.

confirmed: hot8193 exercises 8192+1 jobs for each of ten concentrated experts; hot16384 exercises 8192+8192 with ne == window; the fixture explicitly asserts counts and job total for these cases.
balanced16384 distributes exactly 320 routes to each of 512 experts from the input formula; tail16383 is one row below the maximum; single covers one row.
Every case uses salts 1 and 37. The witness and final output oracle execute on the GPU if run.
256-byte canaries precede/follow each allocation and are checked after drain.
limits: Only concentrated counts/job totals are asserted directly; balanced/single/tail rely more on the final oracle and canaries.
Canaries detect edge writes, not interior corruption or invalid reads.
The final output oracle alone does not close the route false-pass gap described in R975-1.
